correction: The previous 'decode' row (ReadMode::Decode) measured a materialised-dispatch route - the .ekb path-bloom hot array served by OrFs::read - not decoding. ReadMode::Machine is the genuine authoritative machine reconstruction baseline.

passthrough.reason:
fuser 0.15.x exposes no FUSE_PASSTHROUGH init flag, no
             FUSE_DEV_IOC_BACKING_OPEN ioctl and no per-inode backing id, so the
             bundled binding cannot request passthrough (max ABI 7.31)
             even though the kernel is 7.2.9-2-cachyos; a newer fuser or a raw
             ioctl FFI outside the sanctioned modules would be required
passthrough.ekb_is_not_a_valid_backing_file: a .ekb generation has headers/core before the bloom hot blob, so file offset != logical offset; only the certified path-bloom hot array inside it (or a standalone export) is logically aligned

io_uring_fuse.reason: fuser 0.15.1 does not negotiate FUSE-over-io_uring (the FUSE_HAS_IO_URING init flag and per-queue uring setup added in Linux 6.14+); no API is exposed, so the mount uses the classic /dev/fuse request loop.

window_read.name: fuse backing surface (open per read, uncached)

verdict: CORRECTION: for this fully-materialised `Path` object the earlier 'decode' row measured a MATERIALISED-DISPATCH route (the `.ekb` path-bloom `hot` array served by `OrFs::read`), not decoding: it costs 11.0 us per uncached 4 KiB read and 224 us full. Genuine machine decode (`ReadMode::Machine`, authoritative replay from Omega_0 per request with no tile/bloom/block/checkpoint/history route) costs 4182.0 us per uncached 4 KiB read (382x the dispatch) and 30935 us full. The backing surface stays 8.6 us per uncached 4 KiB read; the standalone mapped surface is the resident floor at 0.20 us. Raw file read: 49 us full. FUSE passthrough is NOT available through fuser (max ABI 7.31); kernel 7.2.9-2-cachyos has the passthrough ABI. The `.ekb` is not a valid passthrough backing file (headers/core precede the hot blob), but its path-bloom hot array is logically aligned and is what the backing surface serves.
